messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a few nsys profiles on the long-tail inference job and discovered a weird kernel fragmentation pattern that's triggering misaligned prefetches and kv-cache write serialization. attaching snippets below.

maya: nsys timeline: lots of small flash-attn_v1_small kernels interleaved with large fused-attn kernels. context switch gaps ~120-300us. sm_util oscillates 10%->90% repeatedly.

maya: nvprof summary (reduced):
```
Time(%)  Avg  Name                 Regs  Occ  SMU(%)  Calls
34.1     0.45  flash_attn_v1_small  64    0.12  12.2    12k
41.3     0.89  fused_attn_large     80    0.34  78.6    1.1k
09.2     0.10  kv_cache_read        32    0.05  5.4     24k
```

maya: hypothesis: batching heuristic is picking per-request tile sizes that cause split codepath (small vs large kernels) depending on prefix length distribution. when mixed in the same stream it thrashes shared L2 and causes kv-cache writes to be serialized by the fused kernel's heavy sharedmem usage.

chet: thanks — can you paste the exact heuristic config for that workload? i want to see batch boundaries and tile thresholds.

maya: sure — snippet from runtime config: 
```
batching: {
  max_batch: 64,
  tile_thresholds: [32, 128, 512],
  small_tile_kernel: flash_attn_v1_small,
  large_tile_kernel: fused_attn_large
}
```

maya: also we set kv_cache_write_back: eager by default (write-on-evict disabled).

raj: curious if this is an encoding mismatch — small kernels prefetch 4x stride, large kernels prefetch 8x. when a request crosses the tile_boundary we end up with prefetches targeting overlapping bank sets -> bank conflicts -> stall and later serializing writes.

lucy: can we rerun with two changes: 1) force tile_threshold to [64,256,512] so small kernel is less likely; 2) switch kv_cache_write_back to delayed/batched mode. should be a quick A/B test.

maya: kicked off two traces: 1949991300 (control) and 1949991360 (forced thresholds + delayed write). linking perfetto links: https://perfetto.local/trace/1949991300 , https://perfetto.local/trace/1949991360

perf-bot: trace 1949991300: average p99 latency 54ms, sm_util variance 0.48, nvlink stalls high.

perf-bot: trace 1949991360: average p99 latency 35ms, sm_util variance 0.12, kv_cache write throughput improved x3, no nvlink stall spikes.

maya: quick diff from perfetto flame slices: before => many small flash kernels queued between fused kernels (visible as interleaved red bars). after => fused kernels dominate and small kernel count drops ~80%. also KV write slices moved to batch window and no longer co-located with fused kernels.

chet: omg that's a big win. does unit cost change? any quality/regression concerns?

maya: token cost ~+2% due to slightly larger memory footprint of fused kernel path but latency/cost per request improved because fewer context switches and less serialized IO. output quality identical — same model weights, only kernel selection changed.

raj: two follow-ups: 1) is this workload representative (prefix distribution skew)? 2) can we adaptively change tile_thresholds at runtime based on observed per-route prefix histogram?

lucy: on (1) this customer has heavy short-prefix tail (interactive autocomplete) + occasional long completions. it's the exact mixed distribution that triggers the issue. (2) yes — propose a lightweight route-level sampler that updates thresholds every 10k requests with exponential smoothing.

maya: implementation note: need to guard against thrashing the heuristic itself — add hysteresis and a cooldown window of 30s after changes. also emit a metric: kernel_mix_ratio per route so SRE can alert when mix>0.3 and p99 regresses.

chet: sounds good. can you open a PR with: runtime config defaults -> increase small kernel threshold from 32->64, add kv_cache_write_back: "batched_delayed", and a feature flag runtime.adaptive_tile_thresholds (off by default). include perf traces in the PR.

maya: will do. PR target: eng-runtime/main. attaching minimal repro script for CI profiling:
```
# repro.sh (docker)
docker run --gpus all -v $(pwd):/w redwood/runtime-runner:debug \
  /bin/bash -c "python perf_runner.py --model t5-xl --prefix-dist mixed --batch 48 --trace nsys"
```

ops-bot: created ticket INF-8764 "kernel fragmentation -> adaptive thresholds" assigned to @maya @chet. SLA: normal.

lucy: add a quick dashboard tile: kernel_mix_ratio, kv_write_throughput, sm_util_variance, p99_latency per route. visualizing helped find this.

maya: TL;DR: kernel selection mismatch + eager KV writes caused bank conflicts and write serialization; increasing small-kernel threshold and batching kv writes removed the thrash and cut p99 by ~35%. will open PR and include traces + perfetto links + repro. :rocket:

chet: awesome — thanks team. leave thread updates as PR lands. :thumbsup:
